items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And then, late at night, we'd get Fletcher Henderson and Earl Fatha Hines; we'd get them from the Grand Terrace in Chicago.

ctx.x: Then I had the opportunity to play the World's Fair in 1964, and I told Benny how I used to go to the ice cream parlor and listen to him every Wednesday night at 7:30 on the Camel Caravan -- a show that he broadcast from New York called the Camel Caravan. I'd go over there to the ice cream parlor, and they had a little radio sitting in the window; I'd go over there and listen to him play on the Camel Caravan at ...(?)..

And then, late at night, we'd get Fletcher Henderson and Earl Fatha Hines; we'd get them from the Grand Terrace in Chicago. And we could also get Cab Calloway and Duke Ellington from the Cotton Club, you see... All of this was nationwide radio during those days, you know...
